GAME_PATH.desc: The game's launcher (e.g. Play.exe) - used to open a character's game when it logs in by itself (its Auto login in the panel), at Log in and after a crash.

FIRST_RUN_REPAIR.desc: Repair each character's gear as soon as it's in the game. Off: the first repair waits REPAIR_INTERVAL seconds too.

REPAIR_INTERVAL.desc: Seconds between repairs (VIP Repair All) of each character's gear while Static runs.

ARROWS_MIN.label: Arrows minimum
ARROWS_MIN.desc: The equipped arrows are read from the game's memory; when fewer than this, a pack is taken from the bag or the bank tabs (any pack, full or not) and equipped.

REVIVE_DELAY.desc: Per desktop: once an account is seen dead, wait this long before clicking Revive. Until then that desktop is skipped and the other desktops carry on as usual.

REVIVE_TIME_MULTIPLIER.label: Revive time multiplier
REVIVE_TIME_MULTIPLIER.desc: When the same player kills an account again (several times in a row), the wait before reviving is multiplied by this each time: with 2 it's REVIVE_DELAY, then 2x, 4x... up to MAX_REVIVE_WAIT. 1 = the wait never grows. A kill by a different player starts over at REVIVE_DELAY. Needs the account's character name (Accounts tab).

MAX_REVIVE_WAIT.desc: The longest the multiplied revive wait can get (1800 = 30 minutes). Killed by a monster (told apart from players by the game's memory): revive right away, no message, no notification. See REVIVE_TIME_MULTIPLIER.

ENABLED.desc: When one of your accounts is killed, whisper the killer one chat message, right after that account is revived: click Talk, pick Whisper, type their name in the chat bar's left box and a message in the right box, then Enter. How often a killer gets one: see Send once every day. Kills are read from the game's chat (read-only); needs the account's character name (Accounts tab).

SEND_ONCE_EVERYDAY.label: Send once every day
SEND_ONCE_EVERYDAY.desc: On: each killer gets one message per 24 hours, whichever of your accounts they kill; more kills only make the revive wait grow. Off: they get a message after every revive. Who was messaged is kept in messaged_killers.json next to the settings file (survives restarts).

FORGET_KILLERS.label: Forget killers
FORGET_KILLERS.confirm: Forget every killer that already got a message? They can all get one again.
FORGET_KILLERS.desc: Empties the list of killers who already got a message (messaged_killers.json), so each of them can get a message again. Works right away, even while the script is running.

MESSAGES.desc: One message per line — each reply picks one line at random. English letters, numbers and symbols only (it is typed on a US keyboard).

ENABLED.desc: When a player whispers one of your accounts to start talking (hi, hey, yo...), whisper back a short line after a few seconds, like a person would. Only whispers (not World / Team / Guild). Each player gets one auto reply per Once per player; a talk that goes on is yours to answer from Telegram. Whispers are read from the game's chat (read-only).

AI.label: Answer with AI
AI.desc: Claude writes each reply from the talk so far with that player - short, like a player would type. Whatever only you should answer (a trade, a party, a guild, "are you a bot?", anything it isn't sure of) it leaves to you on Telegram. Staff ([GM], [PM], [PH]) never get an auto reply - they come to Telegram marked STAFF. Off, or with no API key: the rules below.

AI_MODEL.label: AI model
AI_MODEL.desc: Haiku 5.5: fast and very cheap (about $0.00004 a reply) - enough for short chat. Sonnet 5.5 (about $0.0008) and Opus 5.5 (about $0.0016) write more carefully.

API_KEY.label: API key
API_KEY.desc: Your Anthropic API key (console.anthropic.com > Settings > API Keys; billing needs credit). Saved encrypted for this Windows user only - never shown again; paste a new one to change it.

AI_LIMIT.label: AI replies a player
AI_LIMIT.desc: At most this many AI replies to one player within the minutes below - then the talk is left to you on Telegram.

AI_WINDOW.label: ...within
AI_WINDOW.desc: The minutes the limit above counts.

COOLDOWN.label: Once per player
COOLDOWN.desc: Minutes before the same player can get another auto reply.

RULES.default:
hi, hii, hey, hello, helo, yo, hola, salam, slm, hala, heya => what? | hi? | yes? | ? | hey?
bro, dude, man, sir, mate => what? | ? | yes?
sup, wassup, whats up, wsup => nm | nothing u? | ?
how are you, how r u, hru, how are u => fine | good u? | ok
? => ?
RULES.desc: One rule a line: the words a message starts with, then =>, then the replies split by | (one picked at random). Case, punctuation and drawn-out letters are ignored ("HEYYY!!" is "hey"). English letters, numbers and symbols only.

ENABLED.desc: Send Telegram messages to your phone: when one of your accounts is killed, when the script starts, and if it stops with an error. Set up once: in Telegram talk to @BotFather, send /newbot, pick a name, and paste the token it gives you below. Then open your new bot and send it any message (or add it to a group and write there) — that chat gets the notifications. Kills need the accounts' character names (Accounts tab).

BOT_TOKEN.label: Bot token
BOT_TOKEN.desc: The token @BotFather gave you (looks like 1234567890:AAH...). Saved encrypted — never shown again; paste a new one to change it.

NOTIFY.label: Notify on
NOTIFY.desc: Which kills send a message: every kill; only when the same player kills an account again in a row; or only when an account dies 3 or more times within 30 minutes.

ENABLED.desc: Shows the last few console lines on top of the game while static.py runs. Turn off to hide the on-screen console. Clicks always pass through it to the game.

POSITION.desc: Where on the primary screen the on-screen console sits. Move it if it covers a part of the game the scripts need to see.

LINES.desc: How many of the most recent console lines are shown at once.

FONT_SIZE.desc: Text size of the on-screen console.

COLOR.desc: Text color of the on-screen console.

SHADOW.desc: Draw a black drop shadow behind the text, so it stays readable over light parts of the game.

MARGIN.desc: Gap in pixels between the on-screen console and the edge of the screen.

ENABLED.desc: Keeps the grab-arrows and repair countdowns on screen while static.py runs. Turn off to hide them.

POSITION.desc: Where on the primary screen the countdowns sit. Keep it away from the on-screen console and from anything the scripts need to see.

SHADOW.desc: Draw a black drop shadow behind the text, so it stays readable over light parts of the game.

MARGIN.desc: Gap in pixels between the countdowns and the edge of the screen.
